title: The Enhanced Games: A Commercial and Competitive Failure with Broader Industry Implications
summary: The Enhanced Games, a sports competition allowing performance-enhancing drugs, resulted in a $62 million loss for its organizing company, Enhanced Group. Initially hyped as transformative, the event underdelivered competitively and financially. The company, backed by figures like Peter Thiel, pivots to a lower-cost online series. Despite the failure, the peptide and biohacking industry continues to grow, driven by regulatory shifts and Silicon Valley interest.
key_points: The Enhanced Games, a sports event permitting performance-enhancing drugs, posted a $62 million loss for its organizing company, Enhanced Group.
The event was a competitive disappointment, with only one world record broken in swimming.

Enhanced Group, founded in 2023 and valued at $1.2 billion post-IPO, generates revenue primarily through a telehealth platform selling FDA-approved treatments like peptides and testosterone injections.
Most of the company’s Q2 revenue ($17.7 million) came from sponsorships tied to the games, not its core telehealth business.
The company may pivot to a lower-cost online series, *Enhanced Breakers*, due to financial losses.
Despite the Enhanced Games' failure, the peptide and biohacking industry is expanding, supported by regulatory changes under the Trump administration and FDA reclassification of certain substances.
Silicon Valley remains a hub for peptide startups, with companies like Superpower and Noho Labs capitalizing on biohacking trends.
Regulatory frameworks struggle to keep pace with the industry’s rapid growth, posing challenges for oversight.
